memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said, "If I find fifty righteous people in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake." Then Abraham spoke up again: "Now that I have been so bold as to speak to the Lord, though I am nothing but dust and ashes..." - Gen 18:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's answer is immediate and generous: "If I find fifty righteous people... I will spare the whole place for their sake." God does not resist Abraham's plea for mercy; He welcomes it. He is not a reluctant judge who must be talked into kindness, but a God who delights to show mercy and is quick to spare.

This tells us something crucial about God's heart. Sometimes we imagine we must wear God down in prayer, persuading a reluctant deity to be good to us. But Abraham's experience shows the opposite. God is more eager to show mercy than we are to ask for it. As Scripture says, He "delights to show mercy" (Mic 7:18).

Notice also Abraham's beautiful humility: "I am nothing but dust and ashes." Here is boldness and humility held together perfectly. Abraham prays with great confidence, yet without a trace of pride. He knows exactly what he is - dust - and yet he dares to speak to the Lord of all.

This is the posture of true prayer: bold because of who God is, humble because of who we are. We come as "dust and ashes," utterly unworthy, yet welcomed by a God who delights to show mercy. Through Christ, we can "approach God's throne of grace with confidence" (Heb 4:16). Come humbly, but come boldly - you are asking a God who loves to say yes to mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see God as reluctant to show mercy, or delighting in it?
- Can you hold boldness and humility together in your prayers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Merciful God, thank You that You delight to show mercy and welcome my prayers. I come as dust and ashes, unworthy, yet bold because of who You are. Teach me to pray with humble confidence.
Amen.
